(ii) Scholarship money must be used to attend an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana (iii) To remain eligible for scholarships that renew for more than one year, students must remain enrolled consecutively each semester at an accredited post-secondary education institution in Montana.
AFSA awards $1,000 scholarships to 10 students annually. Two Contests. Deadlines August & December Every Year.

A single application opens 60+ LGBTQ+ community scholarship funds for students who are LGBTQ+ or allies and reside in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington. Montana residents are explicitly eligible and may study anywhere; it covers community college, 4-year, and trade/vocational study. The cycle runs roughly October to January.

Point Foundation's flagship national scholarship supports LGBTQ+ students and allies and is open to applicants who are at least a high-school senior. It is a need-based award renewable for up to four years and requires a 3.3 GPA and a demonstrated connection and commitment to the LGBTQ+ community. The window runs September to late November.

rows.source_name: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children

cells.Name of Scholarship: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children
cells.Summary: A $2,000 scholarship for unmarried military dependent children under age 23 with a valid military ID, whose parent is active-duty, Guard/Reserve, retired, or deceased. High-school senior applicants need a 3.0 GPA and full-time enrollment in an accredited 2- or 4-year program.

For children and grandchildren of honorably discharged U.S. veterans or active military, open to 12th graders entering college the fall of their graduation year. Pays $1,000/year (up to $4,000) toward a bachelor's at an accredited 4-year school; requires demonstrated financial need (FAFSA). Window runs January through April 30.

cells.Due Date: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers
cells.Summary: A last-dollar waiver covering in-state tuition for enlisted members of the Montana Army or Air National Guard in good standing who have completed Initial Entry Training. This is not a family benefit — the student themselves must be a Guard member. Apply through your MUS campus.

cells.Due Date: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers
cells.Summary: Waives undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for Montana-resident children (age 25 or under) of service members who were Montana residents at entry to service and were killed in action or died of a service-connected cause. Cannot be combined with other waivers; does not cover fees.

A highly selective last-dollar scholarship for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who are African American, Hispanic American, Native American/Alaska Native, or Asian & Pacific Islander American. Requires a minimum 3.3 weighted GPA and full-time enrollment in a four-year degree. (Active successor to the discontinued Gates Millennium Scholars program.)

Funds undergraduate and graduate study for enrolled Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes (CSKT) members who hold a high-school diploma or GED/HiSET and are accepted to an accredited institution. Reapply each year; applications open in January with a May 1 deadline.

A higher-education grant for enrolled members of the Blackfeet Tribe pursuing an undergraduate degree or certificate at an accredited institution; requires certification of Blackfeet blood. Awards are roughly $2,800–$3,000 with a March 1 deadline. (Confirm amount with the Blackfeet Education Department.)

rows.source_name: Louise A. Dean All Montana Tribal Nations Scholarship

cells.Name of Scholarship: Louise A. Dean All Montana Tribal Nations Scholarship
cells.Summary: A need-based scholarship for members of any Montana tribal nation (Assiniboine, Blackfeet, Gros Ventre, Chippewa Cree, Crow, Kootenai, Little Shell, Northern Cheyenne, Pend d'Oreille, Salish, or Sioux) pursuing a certificate, associate, or bachelor's degree. Open to graduating high-school seniors; requires a 2.25 GPA and proof of financial need. Window Jan 1 to Mar 31.

Covers undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for enrolled members or tribally certified descendants of a federally recognized tribe located in Montana. Requires demonstrated financial need (at least $1 of remaining need) and about 12 months of Montana residency; covers tuition only, not fees. Renewable annually.

A $500 award for graduating high-school seniors (or GED completers), ages 17 to 21, in foster care, kinship care, adoptive, or resource families. Note the gate: the applicant's parent or another supportive adult must be a current NFPA member.

Three annual awards ($1,000 / $750 / $500) for college-bound students who were adopted or spent time in foster care and plan to attend a 4-year college. Selection weighs character, overcoming adversity, and academic progress. Due May 31.

rows.source_name: Montana Foster Youth Higher Education Assistance Program

cells.Name of Scholarship: Montana Foster Youth Higher Education Assistance Program
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply through your MUS campus financial aid office (foster youth / federal Chafee program)
cells.Summary: Last-dollar assistance for Montana foster youth eligible for the federal John H. Chafee program. Must enroll full-time in a degree, vocational, or entry-level professional credential program, have 12 months Montana residency, and have graduated high school or earned an equivalency. Apply through your MUS campus financial aid office.

An achievement- and leadership-based $20,000 award; 150 high-school seniors are selected each year. Open to all graduating seniors (not restricted by background) with a minimum 3.0 GPA. The application window runs August to September 30.

A $20,000 scholarship (plus laptop, textbook credits, and emergency aid) for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who participated in an approved college-readiness program in grades 11-12 and plan to enroll full-time at a four-year college. Rewards persistence over grades — minimum GPA is 2.4. Due February 15. Note the gate: you must have been in an approved college-readiness / college-access program.

For children of service members who died or became seriously injured in the line of duty since 9/11. Administered by Fisher House Foundation through the military scholarship portal (militaryscholar.org); a military-dependent / veteran-family award for graduating seniors entering an accredited college.

cells.Due Date: Annual — closes Mar 15 (apply after fall acceptance)
cells.Summary: For Montana high school seniors from Board of Public Education accredited schools pursuing a qualifying STEM or Healthcare major, enrolling full-time at an eligible Montana campus the fall after graduation. Requires 3.25 cumulative GPA plus 4 years college-prep math and 3 years college-prep science. STEM-focused, renewable annually if requirements are met.

rows.source_name: Montana FFA Foundation Leave a Legacy Scholarship

cells.Name of Scholarship: Montana FFA Foundation Leave a Legacy Scholarship
cells.Summary: Open to any Montana FFA member pursuing post-secondary education or trade/technical school. FFA membership is the gating criterion; a single unified application through the Reach Higher Montana portal qualifies applicants for all Montana FFA Foundation scholarships. Graduating high school FFA seniors are eligible.

cells.Due Date: Annual — closes noon (12 PM) Mon Apr 6, 2026
cells.Summary: Seven $1,000 scholarships for 2026 graduating high school seniors from Flathead, Lake, Missoula, or Ravalli Counties in Montana with a minimum 3.0 GPA, usable toward tuition, books, or expenses at any accredited college or trade school. Local/trades sponsor; apply by emailing the application plus a 500-word essay to Sherry@RhinoRoofingMt.com.

A $1,500 award administered by the Montana Farm Bureau Foundation to assist Montana Farm Bureau members and children of members pursuing higher education. Farm Bureau membership/family affiliation is the gating criterion; agriculture-oriented. Graduating high school seniors who are members or children of members are eligible.

rows.source_name: Montana Farm Bureau Women's Leadership Committee Scholarships

cells.Scholarship Location/Information: Montana Farm Bureau Federation — Women's Leadership Committee
cells.Name of Scholarship: Montana Farm Bureau Women's Leadership Committee Scholarships
cells.Summary: Two $1,500 scholarships from the MFB Women's Leadership Committee, available to both boys and girls graduating high school, who must be a current paid Montana Farm Bureau member or an immediate member of a current paid Montana Farm Bureau family. Agriculture/Farm Bureau affiliation is the gating criterion.

cells.Scholarship Location/Information: Montana FFA Foundation (endowed by Montana Agri-Business Assn. & Montana Grain Elevator Assn.)
cells.Summary: A $500 scholarship for Montana FFA members planning to study agriculture or the agricultural products industry (ag-business, grain industry, agri-business fields). Requires FFA membership and at least 2 years of agricultural education classes. Graduating high school FFA seniors in Montana are eligible; apply via the unified Reach Higher Montana / Montana FFA application.

One online application on the Kaleidoscope portal considers current FFA members for 120+ National FFA scholarships. Graduating high school seniors who are current FFA members qualify (under 23, planning to attend a US college, university, or trade school). Awards run up to $10,000 each.

cells.Due Date: Varies by local EAA chapter (chapters selected annually; no single national deadline)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National; administered through local EAA chapters (student must connect with a participating chapter)
cells.Summary: This aviation scholarship funds up to $12,000 toward a private/sport pilot certificate for youth ages 16-19 (15 for glider). Candidates are selected by a participating local EAA chapter, then screened by EAA — so a Whitefish senior must engage a chapter, complete a Young Eagles flight, and hold a student pilot certificate. High-school seniors in the age range qualify.

rows.source_name: American Welding Society (AWS) Idaho/Montana Section Scholarships

cells.Due Date: Annual — opens Dec 1, closes Mar 1 (for the following fall term)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: Regional — students in Idaho or Montana; AWS Idaho/Montana Section
cells.Name of Scholarship: American Welding Society (AWS) Idaho/Montana Section Scholarships
cells.Summary: The AWS Idaho/Montana Section funds welding/trades students in ID or MT pursuing a welding degree or certificate at a 2-year or 4-year school. A graduating Whitefish senior qualifies as an incoming welding student (AWS requires HS graduate/GED status by the fall term). One AWS Foundation online application at scholarship.aws.org covers National, District, and Section awards.

rows.source_name: Lineman Country Scholarship (Southeast Lineman Training Center)

cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National; Southeast Lineman Training Center (SLTC), Trenton, GA
cells.Name of Scholarship: Lineman Country Scholarship (Southeast Lineman Training Center)
cells.Summary: This trades/lineman scholarship from Southeast Lineman Training Center awards $5,000 (five awards in 2026) to individuals starting a career in the electrical utility/communications lineworker industry. A graduating high school senior or GED holder planning a lineman career qualifies; applicants submit letters of recommendation from three references and an essay to the Scholarship Committee.

cells.Amount: Varies (set yearly by the ILRA Board; covers tuition, textbooks, fees)
cells.Summary: This lineman/trades scholarship is for a son or daughter of a Journeyman Lineman OR someone recommended by one, entering accredited lineman training. Applicants need a high school diploma or GED, so a graduating Whitefish senior qualifies via the family/sponsor connection. Two recommendation letters (one from a HS/GED advisor) and a personal financial-need statement are required.

cells.Due Date: Annual — opens Dec 1, closes Jan 31 (11:59pm CST)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National; open to Eagle Scouts nationwide
cells.Summary: NESA scholarships are for Eagle Scouts and require NESA membership. They explicitly open to graduating high school seniors: Eagle Scouts may apply beginning in their senior year of high school. Awards range from a $5,000 Tappan Scholarship up to a $50,000 four-year Cooke Scholarship ($12,500/yr), with a hard filter on Eagle Scout / Scouting status.

rows.source_name: Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition (Grand Teton Music Festival)

cells.Due Date: Annual — spring (2026 deadline extended to Mon May 18)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: Regional — Wyoming, Idaho, and Montana residents; competition held in Jackson, WY
cells.Name of Scholarship: Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition (Grand Teton Music Festival)
cells.Summary: The Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition is a regional music award open to graduating high school seniors from Wyoming, Idaho or Montana who are pursuing a music degree in college. Montana is explicitly included, so a Whitefish HS senior planning a music degree fits. Selection is by video pre-screen then live semi-final/final rounds, with prizes of $10,000–$25,000.

rows.source_name: ESA Foundation Computer & Video Game Arts Scholarship

cells.Due Date: Annual — opens Apr 1, closes Apr 30 (11:59 PT)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US citizens); administered via Kaleidoscope online portal
cells.Name of Scholarship: ESA Foundation Computer & Video Game Arts Scholarship
cells.Summary: For students pursuing video-game, interactive-entertainment and STEAM careers, this esports/gaming award supports future game creators. Applicants may be graduating HS seniors entering a four-year undergraduate program in fall 2026. Priority to women, nonbinary/gender-nonconforming, or economically disadvantaged applicants.
cells.Focus: Video game arts / STEAM / interactive entertainment

cells.Due Date: Annual — opens Apr 1, closes Apr 30 (11:59 PT)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US citizens); administered via Kaleidoscope online portal
cells.Summary: This esports award supports students competing on or managing a college esports team/club, or those confirmed to compete at the collegiate level in fall 2026. A graduating HS senior can qualify if they are confirmed to compete on a college esports team in fall 2026 (a self-selected filter, not an ineligibility bar). Full-time four-year undergraduate enrollment, min 2.5 GPA, US citizenship, and financial need apply.

cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US high school seniors); mail/email application to VRG, Baltimore, MD
cells.Summary: The Vegetarian Resource Group awards students graduating from US high schools who have promoted vegetarianism/veganism in their schools and communities. This vegetarian/vegan-focused award grants one $10,000 and five $5,000 scholarships. Requires transcripts, three-plus recommendation letters, and an essay on advocacy and goals.

rows.source_name: Duck Brand "Stuck at Prom" Scholarship Contest

cells.Due Date: Annual — submit by early June (2026: Jun 3, 12 PM ET)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US, DC, PR, territories; excludes MD, CO, NE, ND — Montana eligible)
cells.Name of Scholarship: Duck Brand "Stuck at Prom" Scholarship Contest
cells.Summary: This creative/contest scholarship is a photo CONTEST, not a traditional essay scholarship: entrants make and wear original promwear from Duck Tape and submit a photo, judged on creativity and execution. Open to students 14+ enrolled at the high-school level during the 2025-2026 school year. Grand prizes are $10,000 per category with $1,000 runner-up and special-category awards.

cells.Due Date: Annual — closes Feb 14 (not shown on live portal page)
cells.Summary: A single Kaleidoscope portal application covering all Montana 4-H Foundation scholarships for Montana students with 4-H involvement (typically 3+ years in 4-H). 4-H membership is the gating criterion. Applicants complete one application and are matched to the scholarships they qualify for; graduating high school seniors are eligible.

cells.Due Date: Varies (most due senior year of HS, Dec–Apr)
cells.Scholarship Location/Information: National; online portal (futures.pearson.com/scholarships) aggregating FIRST partner scholarships
cells.Summary: The FIRST Scholarship program is a robotics/FIRST portal (hosted on Pearson Futures) linking graduating high school seniors who did FRC/FTC/FLL to 150+ partner scholarships from colleges, businesses, and associations. It is a dynamic portal, not a single award: each scholarship has its own amount, eligibility, process, and deadline. HS seniors are explicitly the target audience.

cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26GBBS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/gbci-leadership-scholarship
cells.Summary: For children, step-children, and employees of Glacier Bancorp (GBCI, headquartered in Kalispell, MT); full- or part-time students eligible. Corporate-sponsor employee/dependent scholarship. Typical award $2,000 per year.

rows.source_name: Dearborn Ranch Montana Game Wardens Scholarship

cells.Name of Scholarship: Dearborn Ranch Montana Game Wardens Scholarship
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26DRSFGW) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/dearborn-ranch-montana-game-wardens-scholarship
cells.Summary: For biological or adopted children of active uniformed Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks Game Wardens (a law-enforcement / first responder family scholarship). Typical award $10,000 per year.

rows.source_name: Dearborn Ranch Montana Highway Patrol Scholarship

cells.Name of Scholarship: Dearborn Ranch Montana Highway Patrol Scholarship
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26DRSFHP) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/dearborn-ranch-montana-highway-patrol-scholarship
cells.Summary: For biological or adopted children of active uniformed Montana Highway Patrol officers (a first responder / law-enforcement family scholarship). Minimum cumulative GPA 2.75. Award $10,000 per year.

cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26KMSE) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/kay-mcmillan-nursing-scholarship
cells.Summary: For graduating seniors enrolling in the pre-nursing program at Montana Tech (or current Montana Tech pre-nursing / nursing students) who show a commitment to community health. Minimum high-school GPA 2.0. Typical award $500–$1,500 per year. Nursing / healthcare focus.

cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26BLAK) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/alan-and-janette-blackburn-scholarship
cells.Summary: Open to any student who graduated or will graduate from a Montana high school, awarded through the Montana Community Foundation. Typical award $500–$1,000 per year. Applies to Whitefish, MT graduating seniors statewide.

rows.source_name: Nep & Mary Ellen Lynch Trade School Scholarship

cells.Name of Scholarship: Nep & Mary Ellen Lynch Trade School Scholarship
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26NMES) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/nep-mary-ellen-lynch-trade-school-scholarship
cells.Summary: For current graduating seniors and past graduates of Montana high schools enrolling full- or part-time at an accredited Montana trade school (cosmetology and massage schools are ineligible). Trade / vocational focus. Typical award $5,000 per year.

rows.source_name: T. Eugene Young Montana's Promise Scholarship

cells.Name of Scholarship: T. Eugene Young Montana's Promise Scholarship
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26TEYS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/t-eugene-young-montanas-promise-scholarship
cells.Summary: For graduating Montana high school seniors pursuing STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) or healthcare degrees to strengthen Montana's workforce. Typical award $1,000–$1,500 per year.

rows.source_name: Reach for the Future Scholarship for Vocational Degree Programs

cells.Name of Scholarship: Reach for the Future Scholarship for Vocational Degree Programs
cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26VMSE2YR) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/reach-for-the-future-scholarship-for-vocational-degree-programs
cells.Summary: For Montana residents (or those with strong Montana ties) enrolled — or seeking enrollment — full-time at a public, private, or tribal college in Montana, studying a vocational or trade program such as aviation technology, carpentry, welding, automobile mechanics, or plumbing. Financial need required. Two-year renewable award, $2,500 per year (must maintain a 2.5 GPA to renew).
cells.Focus: Vocational, Trades (welding, aviation technology, carpentry, plumbing)

cells.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26GOMS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/gary-olszewski-memorial-scholarship
cells.Summary: For students enrolling in a two-year technical / trade program at an accredited school; honors a Montana dryland farmer-tradesman to encourage careers in the trades (carpentry, plumbing, electrical, mechanics). Typical award $8,000 per year for two years. Open statewide, with a preference for Blaine/Hill/Phillips County students.

cells.Amount: $5,000/year, renewable up to 4 years ($20,000 total); up to 100 awards
cells.Summary: National merit scholarship from Equitable (administered by Scholarship America) for U.S. high school seniors with a 2.5+ GPA planning full-time enrollment in a two- or four-year college. $5,000 per year, renewable up to four years ($20,000 total); up to 100 awards. Annual cycle typically opens September and closes December.

cells.Amount: Minimum five awards of $1,000 each (per student)
cells.Summary: National NAEHCY Scholar Fund award for students who are or have been homeless and are McKinney-Vento eligible. Open to college-bound graduating seniors and postsecondary students under 23; a minimum of five $1,000 awards, usable at any accredited U.S. college. 2026 deadline July 31 (recurs annually).
